dod.PhNote: Stable at about 0.0001 to 0.01 M and pH7-8 .5 (Possibly conversion rate too small). Also observed in the corrosion of Cd.

May form solid solutions with Aragonite (Tarnowitzite), due to different crystal structure apparently not with Calcite and Magnesite. At 60C PbMg(CO3)2 is formed (Böttcher 1993) which ist not present in THEREDA.
Crystalline form of Al(OH)3 assumed to be the stable form in cementitious systems. However, microcrystalline or amorphous forms may be relevant as well (see REA1992, MAT/LOT2007, HUM/BER2002).
The solid phase Mg(OH)Cl-2-1-4 appears at T >= 333.15K.
previous name in the former data set: Oxychloride-Mg
high temperature phase of magnesium selenate hydrate
The “aged” (white) solid may be a slightly more ripened form of the hydroxide, or it may be a material with a surface layer of Np2O5, or even incorporating alkali metal ions.
Crystalline MSH phase used by REA1992. Relevance in Mg-bearing cementitious systems not yet clear.
